src/algorithms/edit.c

This file computes four edit costs. The resolver has already removed supported separators and folded ASCII case. Each matrix cell describes a pair of prefixes: the letters read so far from each string. Its value is the cheapest cost of changing one prefix into the other.

Name used below: Optimal String Alignment is the restricted adjacent-letter-swap method. It allows a swap but cannot edit that swapped substring again under its recurrence. Full Damerau-Levenshtein allows further edits. You may see the abbreviations osa and dl in internal adapter names.

Measured observations below describe the recorded dataset and calibrated policy. Timing uses separate synthetic lookup probes; zero observed unsafe matches does not guarantee safety.

Standard-library functions and input bounds

Section titled “Standard-library functions and input bounds”

Standard C99 fmin selects the smallest of the finite nonnegative edit costs. The caller supplies validated strings no longer than KEY_MAX.

Full Damerau-Levenshtein can reuse older matches

Section titled “Full Damerau-Levenshtein can reuse older matches”

The full matrix has an extra border with an unreachable cost. last_row records where each character last occurred in the input; last_matching_column records its latest match in this row. A transposition can jump to that older pair, account for intervening gaps, and swap. This permits ca -> ac -> abc at cost 2. The matrix and indices are local arrays.

Logical prefix cost (i,j) is stored at distance[i+1][j+1]. This offset leaves a guard border for missing earlier matches. last_row[letter] == 0 means that letter has not occurred yet; it must not create a free transposition.

Method Cheapest permitted treatment of ca -> abc Distance
Full Damerau-Levenshtein Swap ca -> ac, then insert b 2
Restricted adjacent swaps Cannot reuse that swapped region for insertion; needs another route 3

Read RapidFuzz’s full-distance example for the distinguishing case, or the Lowrance-Wagner paper for the last-occurrence recurrence. These links explain the distance, not the benchmark’s acceptance thresholds.

Full Damerau-Levenshtein results from this run

Section titled “Full Damerau-Levenshtein results from this run”

Run recorded 2026-11-07 11:27 PST. It recovered 174 of 185 typos. No unsafe acceptance was observed.

It accepted the same inputs as Levenshtein, with about 1.2 times the lookup time. The extra scoring rules added no recovery benefit here.

A median name lookup took about 71 microseconds with 10 properties and 12 milliseconds with 1000. These are separate synthetic typo probes on this host, not timings of the examples below.

Recovered typo: authentiactionserverendpoint resolved to AuthenticationServerEndpoint.

Rejected typo: maximumconcurrentrequestscmunt was intended for MaximumConcurrentRequestsCount. That target ranked first at 0.967, but the runner-up scored 0.933. The 0.033 lead was below the required 0.04, so the resolver declined to guess.

The restricted swap method returns 3 for ca -> abc.17 * Matrix indices are shifted by one; the extra border blocks nonexistent matches.18 * Reference: Lowrance-Wagner, https://doi.org/10.1145/321879.32188019 */20/* measured:ALG03:start - 2026-11-07 recorded run.21 * Recovered 174/185 typos; unsafe accepts 0.22 * Median lookup, 10 properties: about 71 microseconds on this host.23 * Same accepted results as the other edit variants in this run.24 * Input: authentiactionserverendpoint25 * Outcome: correctly resolved to AuthenticationServerEndpoint.26 * Policy limits and comparisons: docs/measured-results.md.27 * measured:ALG03:end */28static double unrestricted_distance(const char *input, const char *candidate) {29    size_t input_length = strlen(input), candidate_length = strlen(candidate);30    size_t input_index, candidate_index;31    unsigned short distance[KEY_MAX + 2][KEY_MAX + 2];32    size_t last_row[128] = {0};33    unsigned short unreachable = (unsigned short)(input_length + candidate_length);3435    /* Logical prefix cost (i,j) lives at [i+1][j+1]. Row/column zero36     * are guards for a letter with no earlier match; row/column one mean empty.37     * Any valid distance is at most input_length + candidate_length. */38    distance[0][0] = unreachable;39    for (input_index = 0; input_index <= input_length; ++input_index) {40        distance[input_index + 1][0] = unreachable;41        distance[input_index + 1][1] = (unsigned short)input_index;42    }43    for (candidate_index = 0; candidate_index <= candidate_length; ++candidate_index) {44        distance[0][candidate_index + 1] = unreachable;45        distance[1][candidate_index + 1] = (unsigned short)candidate_index;46    }47    for (input_index = 1; input_index <= input_length; ++input_index) {48        size_t last_matching_column = 0;49        for (candidate_index = 1; candidate_index <= candidate_length; ++candidate_index) {50            size_t matching_row = last_row[(unsigned char)candidate[candidate_index - 1]];51            size_t matching_column = last_matching_column;52            unsigned short substitution_cost = 1;53            double ordinary_edit, transposition;54            if (input[input_index - 1] == candidate[candidate_index - 1]) {55                substitution_cost = 0;56                last_matching_column = candidate_index;57            }58            {59                double replace_cost = (double)distance[input_index][candidate_index] + substitution_cost;60                double insert_cost = (double)distance[input_index + 1][candidate_index] + 1;61                double delete_cost = (double)distance[input_index][candidate_index + 1] + 1;62                ordinary_edit = fmin(replace_cost, fmin(insert_cost, delete_cost));63            }64            /* Jump to the earlier matching pair, delete/insert the middle, then swap.65             * This can reuse older cells; the restricted method looks two rows back [PM-Os3bF9]. */66            {67                size_t deleted_between = input_index - matching_row - 1;68                size_t inserted_between = candidate_index - matching_column - 1;69                /* Zero occurrence indices lead to the guard border, not a real swap. */70                transposition = (double)distance[matching_row][matching_column] +71                                (double)deleted_between + 1 + (double)inserted_between;72            }73            distance[input_index + 1][candidate_index + 1] =74                (unsigned short)(ordinary_edit < transposition ? ordinary_edit : transposition);75        }76        last_row[(unsigned char)input[input_index - 1]] = input_index;77    }78    return distance[input_length + 1][candidate_length + 1];79}80

Levenshtein reuses prefix costs; the restricted swap method keeps one extra row

Section titled “Levenshtein reuses prefix costs; the restricted swap method keeps one extra row”

For the current cell, the previous row offers deletion, the current row offers insertion, and the diagonal offers keeping or replacing a letter. Only the restricted adjacent-swap method considers the row two positions earlier. Array indices modulo 3 rotate the storage; they do not change the mathematical row number.

Calculate the cell for ca -> cu

Section titled “Calculate the cell for ca -> cu”

The input row counts characters in ca; the candidate column counts characters in cu. Each option finishes those same two prefixes. The neighboring cell has already paid for the smaller problem.

Finish by Saved smaller problem Add now Total
Delete a c -> cu costs 1 1 2
Insert u ca -> c costs 1 1 2
Replace a with u c -> c costs 0 1 1

Store 1. The next t matches in cat -> cut, so the final distance remains 1. The adapter later converts it to similarity 1 - 1/3, about 0.667.

input_index and candidate_index count prefix lengths. Subtract one to read a C character position. current and previous point into existing row buffers; assigning these pointers does not copy rows. Column zero stores the empty-prefix cost. % 3 chooses a reusable buffer, not a different mathematical row.

Lloyd Allison’s explanation connects the three edit choices to neighboring cells and explains row recycling. Jeff Erickson’s chapter, section 3.7, develops prefix alignments. For the extra swap rule, see the restricted-distance reference.

81/** [PM-Lv2pR6] Levenshtein fills a row left to right. Each cell picks the cheapest:82 * previous[j] + 1       delete the input letter83 * current[j-1] + 1      insert the candidate letter84 * previous[j-1] + 0/1   keep or replace the letter85 * Example: cat -> cut costs 1; similarity later becomes 1 - 1/3 [PM-Sc4nV8].86 */87/* measured:ALG01:start - 2026-11-07 recorded run.88 * Recovered 174/185 typos; unsafe accepts 0.89 * Median lookup, 10 properties: about 62 microseconds on this host.90 * Same accepted results as the other edit variants in this run.91 * Input: default request timeout miliseconds92 * Outcome: correctly resolved to DefaultRequestTimeoutMilliseconds.93 * Policy limits and comparisons: docs/measured-results.md.94 * measured:ALG01:end */95static double rolling_distance(const char *input, const char *candidate, int allow_adjacent_swap) {96    size_t input_length = strlen(input), candidate_length = strlen(candidate);97    size_t input_index, candidate_index;98    /* Column zero represents an empty candidate, hence KEY_MAX + 1 columns.99     * Three buffers retain i, i-1 and i-2; ordinary Levenshtein needs only i-1. */100    double rows[3][KEY_MAX + 1];101    for (candidate_index = 0; candidate_index <= candidate_length; ++candidate_index) {102        rows[0][candidate_index] = (double)candidate_index; /* Empty input: insert every letter. */103    }104    for (input_index = 1; input_index <= input_length; ++input_index) {105        /* These pointers select existing arrays. No row is copied or allocated.106         * For i=3, current reuses buffer 0; previous still points to buffer 2. */107        double *current = rows[input_index % 3];108        double *previous = rows[(input_index - 1) % 3];109        current[0] = (double)input_index; /* Empty candidate: delete every input letter. */110        for (candidate_index = 1; candidate_index <= candidate_length; ++candidate_index) {111            /* Indices count prefix letters; C byte positions start one earlier.112             * Each option finishes the SAME pair of prefixes in a different way. */113            int different_letters = input[input_index - 1] != candidate[candidate_index - 1];114            double delete_cost = previous[candidate_index] + 1;115            double insert_cost = current[candidate_index - 1] + 1;116            double replace_cost = previous[candidate_index - 1] + (different_letters ? 1 : 0);117            /* Worked cell, ca -> cu:118             * delete a: cost(c,cu)+1 = 1+1 = 2119             * insert u: cost(ca,c)+1 = 1+1 = 2120             * replace a: cost(c,c)+1 = 0+1 = 1. Keep the cheapest: 1.121             * The next t/t in cat -> cut adds zero, so the final distance is 1. */122            current[candidate_index] = fmin(delete_cost, fmin(insert_cost, replace_cost));123            /* [PM-Os3bF9] The restricted method handles crossed letters with one swap.124             * ab -> ba costs 1 instead of 2. Three rows retain the i-2 cell.125             * Unlike [PM-Dl8xA4], this recurrence cannot re-edit that substring. */126            /* measured:ALG02:start - 2026-11-07 recorded run.127             * Recovered 174/185 typos; unsafe accepts 0.128             * Median lookup, 10 properties: about 71 microseconds on this host.129             * Same accepted results as the other edit variants in this run.130             * Input: authentiactionserverendpoint131             * Outcome: correctly resolved to AuthenticationServerEndpoint.132             * Policy limits and comparisons: docs/measured-results.md.133             * measured:ALG02:end */134            if (allow_adjacent_swap && input_index > 1 && candidate_index > 1) {135                int letters_cross = input[input_index - 1] == candidate[candidate_index - 2] &&136                                    input[input_index - 2] == candidate[candidate_index - 1];137                if (letters_cross) {138                    double swapped = rows[(input_index - 2) % 3][candidate_index - 2] + 1;139                    if (swapped < current[candidate_index]) current[candidate_index] = swapped;140                }141            }142        }143    }144    return rows[input_length % 3][candidate_length];145}146

Dispatch the three unit-cost distances

Section titled “Dispatch the three unit-cost distances”

Mode 2 uses the full matrix. Modes 0 and 1 share rolling rows; only mode 1 enables adjacent swaps. The distinguishing test is ca versus abc: full Damerau-Levenshtein returns 2 and the restricted method returns 3. The restricted method cannot repeatedly edit the same substring under its recurrence.

147/** mode 0=Levenshtein, 1=restricted adjacent swaps, 2=full Damerau-Levenshtein. */148double edit_distance(const char *input, const char *candidate, int mode) {149    if (mode == 2) return unrestricted_distance(input, candidate);150    return rolling_distance(input, candidate, mode == 1);151}152

Assign global typing costs before filling weighted rows

Section titled “Assign global typing costs before filling weighted rows”

Equal bytes cost zero. A substitution involving a digit costs 2. Horizontal neighbors in the three listed QWERTY rows cost 0.5; other letters cost 1. Insertions and deletions also cost 2 for digits. Two rolling rows retain fractional costs. These are global rules, not exceptions for particular properties.

Calculate weighted cost before normalization

Section titled “Calculate weighted cost before normalization”
Names Replace Delete then insert Chosen cost Similarity
a, s 0.5 2 0.5 1 - 0.5/1 = 0.5
v1, v2 2 4 2 1 - 2/3, about 0.333

The denominator is the larger weighted length, not byte length. v1 has weight 1 + 2 = 3. The recurrence is a weighted version of the edit calculation above; these keyboard and digit prices are project choices.

No property-specific exceptions.155 */156/* measured:ALG04:start - 2026-11-07 recorded run.157 * Recovered 174/185 typos; unsafe accepts 0.158 * Median lookup, 10 properties: about 330 microseconds on this host.159 * Same accepted results as the other edit variants in this run.160 * Input: apiendpoinqv2161 * Outcome: correctly resolved to ApiEndpointV2.162 * Policy limits and comparisons: docs/measured-results.md.163 * measured:ALG04:end */164static double substitution_cost(char input, char candidate) {165    const char *keyboard_rows[] = {"qwertyuiop", "asdfghjkl", "zxcvbnm"};166    size_t row;167    if (input == candidate) return 0;168    if (isdigit((unsigned char)input) || isdigit((unsigned char)candidate)) return 2;169    for (row = 0; row < 3; ++row) {170        const char *input_key = strchr(keyboard_rows[row], input);171        const char *candidate_key = strchr(keyboard_rows[row], candidate);172        if (input_key && candidate_key) {173            int adjacent_keys = input_key - candidate_key == 1 || candidate_key - input_key == 1;174            if (adjacent_keys) return 0.5;175        }176    }177    return 1;178}179180/** Same row movement as [PM-Lv2pR6], but each move has a typing cost. */181double weighted_distance(const char *input, const char *candidate) {182    size_t input_length = strlen(input), candidate_length = strlen(candidate);183    size_t input_index, candidate_index;184    double rows[2][KEY_MAX + 1];185    rows[0][0] = 0;186    for (candidate_index = 1; candidate_index <= candidate_length; ++candidate_index) {187        rows[0][candidate_index] = rows[0][candidate_index - 1] +188                                  (isdigit((unsigned char)candidate[candidate_index - 1]) ? 2 : 1);189    }190    for (input_index = 1; input_index <= input_length; ++input_index) {191        double *current = rows[input_index % 2];192        double *previous = rows[(input_index - 1) % 2];193        /* Operation price is local; a cell stores the accumulated cheapest cost. */194        double deletion_cost = isdigit((unsigned char)input[input_index - 1]) ? 2 : 1;195        current[0] = previous[0] + deletion_cost;196        for (candidate_index = 1; candidate_index <= candidate_length; ++candidate_index) {197            double insertion_cost = isdigit((unsigned char)candidate[candidate_index - 1]) ? 2 : 1;198            double delete_total = previous[candidate_index] + deletion_cost;199            double insert_total = current[candidate_index - 1] + insertion_cost;200            double replace_total = previous[candidate_index - 1] +201                                   substitution_cost(input[input_index - 1], candidate[candidate_index - 1]);202            /* a -> s: replacement .5 beats delete+insert 2.203             * v1 -> v2: replacement 2 beats digit delete+insert 4. */204            current[candidate_index] = fmin(delete_total, fmin(insert_total, replace_total));205        }206    }207    return rows[input_length % 2][candidate_length];208}
